messages:
Alex: Quick sync — noticed a 5-8% tail latency bump in the small-batch chat job after the runtime 2.1 patch. Metric points to more time in kernel scheduling. Did anyone run low-overhead vs full traces in staging?
Ravi: I ran both yesterday. TL;DR: full nsys (system+cuda) trace shows ~+18% CPU and ~+30% end-to-end for a 60s capture on our microbench; nsys sampling mode (–sample) landed around +3% to +5%.
Julie: interesting. Are we sure it's profiler overhead and not the new kernel-selection fallback creating more tiny kernels? More small kernels = more context switches + profiler hits.
Ravi: yeah that's the suspicion. I compared a kernel timeline: without profiler we had long contiguous kernels for attention; with full trace the timeline fragmented into many tiny launches, probably due to timing noise.
Simon: can you paste the commands you ran?
Ravi: sure:
```
# full nsys capture (heavy)
nsys profile --output=run_full --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --duration=60 \ 
  --sample=none --target-processes=all --capture-range=none --force-overwrite \n\n# sampling mode (lighter)
nsys profile --output=run_sample --sample=cpu --trace=cuda --duration=60 
```
Alex: any perfetto runs? I want something we can ship to customers / use in private safely.
Ravi: perfetto via android/perfetto collector + ring buffer is much lighter. I did a 2-minute perfetto sampling run — overhead ~+1.5% on the same workload. But perfetto misses some CUDA context details unless we enable special connector.
Julie: reminder: kernel-selection changes made the runtime emit more small kernels (merged/unmerged transpose kernels). That amplifies sampling noise: even a 1% overhead per kernel accumulates.
perf-bot: [auto] profiling-safety-check: staging capture size=60s, estimated cost +0.04 tokens, recorded 2.1MB of metadata.
Simon: we need concrete guardrails before enabling any automated profiler in prod. Proposed set: 1) default to sampling-only mode (no syscall + no full cuda tracing) 2) per-request duration cap (30s) 3) rate limit to 0.5% of traffic or 1 capture/min per host 4) automatic disable if observed tail-latency delta > 4% in 5m window 5) opt-in env var REDWOOD_SAFE_PROFILER=true
Alex: +1. Also add a circuit-breaker that disables profiler if observed an increased kernel-launch rate (since that spikes profiler overhead).
Ravi: I can instrument a small metric: kernel_launches_per_sec and compare vs baseline moving-avg. If launch rate increases 2x while profiler enabled -> auto-disable. We can expose this via /debug/profiler-state.
Julie: for data collection, prefer perfetto traces shipped compressed. Add a small uploader that only sends very small sample sets to s3 and auto-delete after 7 days.
Simon: for debugging sessions we should have a quick checklist: why use full vs sample, expected overhead, capture duration, target workload, privacy checklist. I'll draft one.
Alex: action items:
- Ravi: prototype kernel_launches_per_sec metric + auto-disable logic (due EOD Thu) :point_right:
- Simon: doc + checklist for safe-profile runbooks (due Mon)
- Julie: add telemetry for small-kernel churn (emit histogram of kernel durations) (due Fri)
- Ops: add env var gate + 0.5% traffic rate limiter in canary pipeline
Ravi: quick numbers I measured (microbench, 8xA100, batch=2, seq=512):
  - baseline (no profiler): p50=12ms p95=45ms p99=86ms
  - perfetto sampling (2m): p50=12.1ms p95=46ms p99=88ms (+2% tail)
  - nsys sampling: p99=90ms (+4.7%)
  - nsys full capture: p99=111ms (+29%)
Julie: thanks — that p99 jump with full capture is unacceptable for any auto-enabled profiling.
perf-bot: [auto] suggestion: enable sampling mode + kernel_launches_per_sec heuristic.
Alex: agreed. Let's avoid full nsys in prod; reserve for offline deeper investigations on reproducer. If someone needs full captures we require an explicit opt-in with runbook and canary tag.
Ravi: I'll push a safe_profiler flag in the runtime that defaults to sampling and implements the circuit-breaker. Will add metrics and log lines: `profiler=enabled mode=sampling baseline_launch_rate=123`
Simon: nice. When you have a branch ping me and I'll review the checklist + runbook.
Julie: small ask — add an internal dev-experiment to see if kernel coalescing reduces small-kernel churn; that should reduce profiler sensitivity and overall tail latency.
Alex: all good. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Simon: cc @perf-bot for follow-up alerting and a weekly summary of profiler toggles.
Ravi: will post short write-up with numbers and the nsys/perfetto commands in eng-runtime wiki later today.
Alex: closing thread — we'll follow up in the PR and the runbook doc.
